Finding high-quality, free 3D game assets has become incredibly accessible, with many professional artists and platforms releasing production-ready models. 

To help you find exactly what you need for your game’s visual style, here are the best sites to find free 3D game assets, categorized by type.

---

### 1. Stylized & Low-Poly Assets (Best for Prototyping, Jams, & Indie Games)
If you are building a low-poly, stylized, or casual game, these creators and platforms offer thousands of cohesive, beautifully designed assets.

*   **Kenney.nl (The "Patron Saint" of Game Dev):** Kenney has released over 40,000 game assets completely free under a **CC0 (Public Domain)** license, meaning you can use them in commercial games without even needing to give credit. 
    *   *What you’ll find:* Low-poly vehicles, modular dungeon pieces, nature, weapons, and characters.
*   **Quaternius (quaternius.com):** A highly popular independent artist who releases massive, fully-rigged and textured 3D asset packs.
    *   *What you’ll find:* Modular character outfits, fantasy props, medieval villages, stylized nature, and a massive "Universal Animation Library" containing hundreds of game-ready animations (all CC0).
*   **Kay Lousberg (KayKit on itch.io):** Kay creates exceptionally cute, polished, and modular stylized low-poly kits. 
    *   *What you’ll find:* Dungeon packs, medieval character packs (fully rigged), animations, sci-fi bits, and survival game resources.
*   **itch.io (Free Game Assets Section):** By navigating to `itch.io/game-assets/free`, you can browse thousands of indie-created 3D assets. It is one of the best places to find unique, stylized packs that aren't on mainstream storefronts.

---

### 2. High-Fidelity & Photorealistic Assets (Best for Realistic & AAA-Style Games)
If you are developing a realistic, high-fidelity game, these sites host industry-standard, photorealistic models.

*   **Fab (Epic Games - fab.com):** Epic Games merged the Unreal Engine Marketplace, Sketchfab, ArtStation Marketplace, and Quixel Megascans into one unified platform. It is an absolute powerhouse for game developers.
    *   *What you’ll find:* Filter by "Free" to find thousands of 3D models. Furthermore, Epic hosts a **"Limited-Time Free"** section where premium, paid 3D environment and prop packs are made free to claim permanently every two weeks.
    *   *Quixel Megascans on Fab:* Access thousands of ultra-realistic, scanned materials, 3D foliage, and props. *(Note: Megascans are generally free to use, but check if licensing limits their use specifically to Unreal Engine).*
*   **Poly Haven (polyhaven.com):** A community-funded platform that provides incredibly high-quality, PBR-ready 3D models, textures, and HDRIs.
    *   *What you’ll find:* Highly optimized, realistic props, architecture, and outdoor elements. Every single file on Poly Haven is **CC0**.

---

### 3. General 3D Repositories & Engine Stores
These platforms are major marketplaces where individual creators upload free samples of their work.

*   **Unity Asset Store:** If you use Unity, this is a must-visit. By filtering search results to "Free Assets," you can download thousands of Unity-optimized packages. They also run a "Publisher of the Week" promotion which often gives away high-quality paid assets for free.
*   **CGTrader & TurboSquid:** These are primarily commercial storefronts for professional 3D artists, but both feature massive libraries of free models. 
    *   *Pro tip:* Use their search filters to sort by "Free" and filter by maximum polygon count to ensure the models are optimized for real-time game engines.
*   **OpenGameArt.org:** An old-school, community-driven database for open-source game assets. While the search UI is outdated, it is a goldmine for finding hidden gems, retro 3D models, and sound effects under various Creative Commons licenses.

---

### ⚠️ A Quick Warning on Licensing
Before importing any free asset into your game, **always check the license**:
1.  **CC0 (Public Domain):** You can do whatever you want—use commercially, modify, and distribute without attribution.
2.  **CC-BY (Attribution):** Free to use commercially, but you **must** credit the creator in your game's credits.
3.  **Engine-Specific Licenses:** Assets downloaded from the Unreal Engine / Fab "Epic Games Content" section are sometimes restricted for use **only within Unreal Engine**. Make sure you read the fine print if you plan on exporting them to Unity, Godot, or another engine.
